questions.question: Describe how Britain raised volunteers in 1914 and 1915.
questions.expected_answer: With a small professional army, Britain relied on Lord Kitchener's call for volunteers; about 750 000 joined by the end of September 1914 and about two and a half million by early 1916, for reasons including patriotism, anger at events in Belgium, adventure, the belief in a short war, pressure and pay. Pals battalions let friends serve together but meant whole towns could lose their men in one battle. About a quarter of a million under-age boys served, and the Order of the White Feather pressured men out of uniform. South Africa and Australia relied entirely on volunteers.

questions.question: Explain why Britain introduced conscription and the arguments about it.
questions.expected_answer: Volunteer numbers fell while casualties rose, so the Military Service Act of January 1916 conscripted unmarried men and widowers without children aged 18 to 41, extended to married men in May 1916 and later to age 51. Essential workers, the unfit, those supporting dependants, ministers and conscientious objectors could apply to local tribunals for exemption. Supporters said it shared the burden and was needed to win; opponents said it violated individual freedom and conscience. It was not applied to Ireland in 1916, and the 1918 attempt caused protest.

questions.question: Describe wartime propaganda and censorship and the treatment of conscientious objectors.
questions.expected_answer: Propaganda, deliberately one-sided information, used posters such as Kitchener's and Daddy, what did YOU do in the Great War?, atrocity stories mixing real and exaggerated events in Belgium, images of Germans as Huns, and films such as The Battle of the Somme; DORA in 1914 allowed censorship of newspapers and letters. About sixteen thousand objectors, many Quakers, faced hostile tribunals; some did non-combatant or civilian work, while absolutists were court-martialled and imprisoned in harsh conditions, some sentenced to death and reprieved, dozens died, and they lost the vote for five years.
